checks.name: a4-workspace-pinning-and-the-measured-dir-question
checks.summary: The one question left open about the argv was whether --dir (opencode) and -C (codex) are a double expression of Invocation.WorkingDirectory. MEASURED ANSWER: they are not. internal/runner/supervisor.go's ProcessSupervisor.Run takes only a context and an argv and never assigns a working directory to the child -- there is no assignment to a command directory anywhere in the file. internal/runner/provider.go's SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run never reads Invocation.WorkingDirectory either; it reads Argv, Stdin and Environment. So on the production path Invocation.WorkingDirectory is currently consumed by nothing at all, and for codex and opencode the flag is the ONLY representation of the workspace that reaches the child process. Deleting it would leave the child running in whatever directory the runner happened to be in. This refutes dp-v2-027 d3's rationale, which states that ProcessSupervisor sets the child directory. Editing internal/runner to consume the field is outside this task's allowed paths. The flags therefore stay. MEASURED DISCREPANCY with A4 as written, recorded rather than weakened silently: A4 asks for 'no argv element is an absolute path other than argv[0]', which cannot hold while the workspace argument exists. The assertion is made stronger where it can be instead: WorkingDirectory equals the request workspace for all three adapters; argv[0] is a bare executable name and is NOT an absolute path (the runner resolves it to the approved preflight record's executable path and refuses when the two disagree); the workspace appears at most once in argv; it must immediately follow that adapter's measured directory flag; codex and opencode carry exactly one absolute path and claude carries zero; no argv element carries a NUL, a carriage return, a newline or a path traversal segment; and Build refuses six distinct bad workspaces covering all four shapes. What holds the boundary is recorded: internal/runner.NamespaceConfinement pins the writable mount at the workspace with a rootless user and mount namespace and refuses to start the child when the kernel cannot provide it, and ProcessSupervisor runs the child in its own process group and terminates the group TERM then KILL. The adapter's job is only to be unable to ask to leave.

checks.name: a5-a6-nine-case-fixture-matrix-as-one-table-over-three-adapters
checks.summary: validation.md's nine rows taken verbatim, with two rows split because each names two distinguishable facts: 'empty/malformed structured output' becomes two files and 'usage obtainable/not obtainable' becomes two files. The timeout/cancel row has no file at all, because a timeout and a cancellation are conditions of the invocation rather than shapes of an output; they are driven through ClassifyError and NormalizeError, and the absence of any timeout- or cancel-named file in testdata is itself asserted. Ten cases times three adapters is 30 cells, and every cell asserts Succeeded, FailureClass, Retryable, Ambiguous, UsageReported and whether an output digest is present. Per-cell expectations: success and the two usage cases succeed with no class; model-error and zero-exit-error-envelope give provider-model not retryable; usage-exhaustion gives provider-quota retryable; non-zero-exit gives provider-transport retryable; empty-structured-output, malformed-structured-output and cli-version-incompatible give contract-incompatible not retryable. DISTINCT TABLE DRIVERS OVER THIS MATRIX: 1, asserted from the AST. fixtureMatrix is declared exactly once and exactly one range statement in the whole package drives it. Three near-identical copies would satisfy every assertion above while defeating the purpose, which is that a change to build, parseFixture or normalize visibly reaches all three adapters; every cell therefore routes through the single exported entry point ParseOrClassify. A6 representation: one additive boolean Result.UsageReported with the JSON key usage_reported, set by parseFixture from a pointer-typed fixture usage field. It changes no existing assertion about Result.Usage: Usage still carries exactly the counts the fixture declared and a fixture with no usage object still yields the Usage zero value, which is what the pre-existing assertion in TestAdaptersBuildSafeArgvAndParseMetadata checks. The two usage fixtures are asserted to have IDENTICAL Usage values and different UsageReported values, so the distinction is provably about reporting and not about counts. The usage window treats the unreported case as unknown, never as zero consumption.

checks.name: a9-provider-account-pool
checks.summary: Exactly three slots keyed by codex, claude and opencode. No fourth slot is constructible: a four-key seed, a two-key seed and a seed with a misspelled name are all refused, the slot map is unexported, and a fourth name resolves to no slot. No fourth adapter type was added, so V2-067's assertion that the declared adapter types are exactly three still holds unchanged. WHAT A SLOT HOLDS, asserted as an exact field set with reflect so a ninth field fails the test: Name, Authorized, VerifiedByLoopInvocation, PreflightRecordID, CooldownDeadline, ConsecutiveFailures, LastFailureClass, State. WHAT A SLOT DOES NOT HOLD: no credential value, no environment value, no authentication token, no session identifier, no owner identity, no executable path, no threshold number. The slot has exactly ONE numeric field and it is asserted to be ConsecutiveFailures, so there is nowhere to copy a limit to. The preflight record is referenced by id only and nothing is copied out of it: the credential already has exactly one home in the runner's Secret Broker, and the executable path's authority is the digest-bound approved record that CostLedger.Reserve checks argv[0] against, so a second copy could only diverge silently. Acquire and Release take an explicit time argument, asserted on the method signatures, and the package reads no clock in any non-test file, asserted by the determinism scan. Transitions whose meaning does not depend on time deliberately do not take one, so an ignored argument cannot be mistaken for a recorded timestamp. A second Acquire of an in-use slot is refused and never queued; Release of a slot nobody holds is refused; Release under a stale lease serial is refused. The per-Provider concurrency ceiling is one BY CONSTRUCTION: an AST scan asserts that Acquire is the only function in the package whose results include a Lease, so there is no code path that returns two live handles for one name. Another Provider is unaffected, so the ceiling is per Provider and not global. Quarantined, stopped-for-inspection and unauthenticated slots are moved by no deadline and no probe -- a cooldown, an elapsed thousand hours and a probe issuance are each refused -- and only an explicit external clearance moves them. A Provider the standing authorization does not cover rests unauthenticated and cannot be cleared by the Loop at all.

checks.name: a10-per-provider-usage-window
checks.summary: THE THREE-WAY DISTINCTION, stated as required. internal/quota is the Firestore daily free-tier reservation: its unit is Firestore reads, writes and deletes, its owner is the datastore, and its failure meaning is that this Loop would exceed the free tier today. This task does not edit it, and this window does not reuse it. internal/runner.CostLedger is the runner-local, owner-approved, fail-closed runaway detector, and it alone has the authority to decide, before exec, whether a process may start; docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md records its purpose as a runaway detector and never a billing rule, and records its observation boundary. internal/provider.UsageWindow is neither: it counts, per Provider and per named window, the invocations the Loop attempted through the pool and the token counts a Provider reported, and it is an input to breaker and pool selection and nothing else. It NEVER decides whether a process may start, and it NEVER claims to know a subscription's remaining allowance -- the population it counts is only what this Loop invoked, a strict subset of what the subscription was used for, so such a claim would be false in the only case that matters. Both refusals are asserted structurally: no method name on the window reads as an authority to start or settle, and no field of its report reads as remaining, allowance, balance or quota. MONETARY VOCABULARY BAN: usd, cost, price, billing, spend and credit, plus the seventh word this record cannot spell without violating its own rule, are checked case-insensitively as substrings over every identifier the AST finds in every non-test file of the package and over the marshalled JSON keys of 16 emitted types. The scan has a positive control over seven known-bad names. The provider-side spelling of the exhaustion FailureClass is unchanged; it is not one of the banned words. Exhaustion is reached exactly one unit over the ceiling and not before, measured on both axes: with an invocation ceiling of three, the third attempt is within-window and the fourth is exhausted; with a token ceiling of one hundred, exactly one hundred reported is within-window and one hundred and one is exhausted. A window with an implicit no-ceiling cannot be constructed, so exhaustion is never unreachable. Rollover is driven by the caller's time argument and never by a stored clock: one second before the window length the generation is unchanged and the state is unchanged, at the length the generation advances by one, and four periods passed at once advance it by four. The state set is exactly within-window, exhausted and unknown. An unreported usage makes the token side unknown and contributes zero tokens; a reported usage of all zeroes leaves the window within-window. An already established invocation-count exhaustion stays exhausted even when the token side is unknown.

checks.name: a11-circuit-breaker-opening-table
checks.summary: The breaker switches on internal/provider's own FailureClass and does not import internal/domain, so the provider component gains no dependency edge and stays a leaf. The Loop-level mapping is a declared table in the test and in the runbook only. PROVIDER-LOCAL ROWS, nine, each asserted for behaviour and not only for the label: provider-quota opens immediately; contract-incompatible opens immediately; provider-transport counts toward a windowed count; timeout counts toward the same count and marks any resulting open ambiguous; unknown counts at a strictly higher count and never opens on a first occurrence; provider-model opens only the narrower Provider-and-model circuit and leaves the Provider circuit sending, with another model in the same pool asserted to stay sending; provider-unauthenticated moves the pool slot to unauthenticated without opening; cancelled neither counts nor opens; invalid-input neither counts nor opens. LOOP-LEVEL DECLARED ROWS, seventeen, asserted to be seventeen and free of duplicates: provider-quota and contract-incompatible open immediately; provider-transport and unknown count; provider-model opens the narrower circuit; secret-suspected moves the slot to quarantined; the reached-limit class moves the slot to stopped-for-inspection; and invalid-input, policy-denied, capacity-unavailable, execution-lost, progress-stalled, verification-failed, external-ambiguous, integration-conflict, preview-regression and promotion-partial neither count nor open. provider-unauthenticated is deliberately NOT one of the seventeen: V2-067 added it to internal/provider rather than to the Loop-level taxonomy, and its row is in the provider-local table. EXHAUSTIVENESS VERDICT: exhaustive over the provider-local class set BY CONSTRUCTION. The FailureClass constants are read out of the package's own AST and compared against both FailureClasses() and the opening table's key set, so a tenth class added without a row fails the test in two places. A class with no row is refused with a named error rather than defaulting. The two Loop-level conditions that are not adapter classifications arrive through explicit pool calls rather than through a FailureClass, and in both cases the circuit is asserted to stay sending, because neither is an observation about the Provider: a suspected secret exposure quarantines the slot, and a reached runaway-detector limit stops it for inspection -- reaching a limit is a stop for inspection, never a success and never a failure, so opening on it would report a Provider fault for a Loop-side stop. progress-stalled has its own assertion of ABSENCE: it is not a provider-local class, it has no row in the provider-local table, asking for one is refused, and its declared Loop-level row records why -- it routes to checkpoint, TERM/KILL and a new Execution, it does not name the Provider, and opening a circuit on it would take a working Provider out of service on evidence about something else.

checks.name: a12-closing-is-never-time-alone
checks.summary: VERDICT: there is no path by which elapsed time alone returns a circuit to sending. Asserted directly, for every way a circuit can open, by advancing the caller's time by a minute, an hour, a day and thirty days with no probe and no reported success and requiring that the state never reads as sending. open to half-open requires all of: the cooldown deadline passed under the caller's time argument (nine minutes into a ten-minute cooldown is refused, ten minutes exactly is allowed); the open being probe-eligible at all; when the open was caused by an exhaustion class, the usage window having ALSO rolled over; and the pool issuing the single outstanding probe. Exactly one probe can be outstanding at a time, across the whole pool: while one is held, a second for the same Provider and a second for a different Provider are both refused. The exhaustion case is proven with the case that a time-only close gets wrong: a one-day window and a ten-minute cooldown, so the deadline passes at thirty minutes while the window has not rolled. No probe is issued at thirty minutes and none at twenty-three hours, and none is left outstanding by the refusal; the probe becomes available only at twenty-four hours when the window rolls. Elapsed time does not make an exhausted window fresh, and a timed probe against one is a guaranteed second exhaustion that spends a real invocation to learn nothing. half-open reaches closed only on a reported successful observation, never on issuing the probe: the state immediately after issuing is probing, and only ApplySuccess returns it to sending, at which point the probe is returned to the pool and the slot is marked verified. A failed probe multiplies the cooldown up to the declared ceiling and does not reset the counter: ten minutes, then thirty, then ninety which is the ceiling, then ninety again, with the pool's consecutive-failure count asserted to advance across the failed probe rather than reset. A stale probe cannot report an outcome. A contract-incompatible open is never probe-eligible: probes at one hour, one day and one year are all refused, because nothing about waiting changes either side's declared version. It closes only on an explicitly observed CHANGE of declared CLI version; observing the same version does not close it. A quarantined or stopped-for-inspection slot has no probe and no deadline that can move it, asserted in the pool item above. Every one of these is driven by an injected time argument. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine exists anywhere in the package.

checks.name: a13-an-open-breaker-does-not-read-as-a-broken-provider
checks.summary: The exported state set is exactly sending, not-sending and probing, each naming this Loop's own action. All three are asserted reachable and every state the breaker reports is asserted to be one of them. No identifier in any non-test file of the package is named healthy, unhealthy, broken, down, up, alive, dead or ok. Every not-sending and probing value carries the closed set of failure classes that produced it (each asserted to be a declared class), the name of the window the count was taken over, and an observation_scope value. A sending value carries none of them, because there is no declined decision to justify. The observation_scope value is the package's single declared constant and is asserted to say, in words, that only invocations that passed through this Loop's own execution path were counted and that an invocation a person or another process started directly against the same CLI is not in this population and cannot be seen. MEASURED PRECEDENT recorded, from docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md's observation-boundary section: the runner's ledger records an invocation only when it passed through SupervisedInvocationRunner and CostLedger.Reserve, and the recorded example is that six real claude invocations run by hand from a shell during V2-017 -- two checking a minimal HOME and PATH configuration, four checking behaviour against an unreachable URL -- appear nowhere in it, while the ledger holds only the eight invocations and eleven entries that went through the harness. A breaker built on the same population therefore knows how this Loop's own calls went and nothing about the Provider's condition, which is exactly why a field named healthy would be false in the only case that matters.

checks.name: a14-handoff-conversion
checks.summary: PrepareHandoff keeps its existing meaning and its existing assertion inside TestFailureClassificationAndHandoff passes unchanged. Added: Handoff.Validate; HandoffContentDigest over IncrementID, Constraints, Decisions, Artifacts, Verification and Unresolved, marshalled in a fixed field order over slices and never maps so the digest is deterministic; RequestFromHandoff; ChainHandoff; and a bounded closed-enum attempt history. SIX ORDERED PAIRS VERDICT: all six of codex-claude, codex-opencode, claude-codex, claude-opencode, opencode-codex and opencode-claude convert, and the target Request's packet compares equal to the source packet field by field, enumerated by name through reflection so a field added to WorkPacket later is not silently unchecked, including every Artifact name and digest and every Verification entry. DIGEST FAIL-CLOSED VERDICT: twelve distinct mutations between PrepareHandoff and RequestFromHandoff are each refused rather than silently accepted -- the Increment id, a dropped constraint, a REORDERED constraint list, a dropped decision, a changed decision detail, a dropped Artifact, a changed Artifact name, a changed Artifact digest, a dropped Verification entry, a changed Verification status, a changed Verification evidence digest, and a cleared unresolved list. Blanking the carried digest is refused too, so the check cannot be skipped by deleting what it checks against. Changing a field the digest is declared NOT to cover does not fabricate a mismatch. RequestFromHandoff refuses a target outside the three names, at both PrepareHandoff and conversion time; refuses when the target's breaker is not sending; and refuses when it is probing, which is not sending either -- one invocation is already committed to finding out and a handoff is not that invocation. The same handoff converts once the target is sending again, which proves the refusal was about the circuit and not about the handoff. PING-PONG VERDICT: a two-hop chain preserves the first failure class in the history, and handing the same Increment back to a Provider already present in the history is refused in all three directions -- back to the origin, back to the middle Provider, and as a third hop. A different Increment restarts the history, because it is a different question. The bound is stated: MaxHandoffHistory is 2, which is not arbitrary -- with three Provider names and the no-revisit rule a chain can contain at most two handoffs -- and a history past it is refused by an explicit length check as well as by the rule. Handoff's only string-typed fields are asserted to be exactly the contract version, the two Provider names and the two digests, and no field of either type may be named for a prompt, response, conversation, transcript, session, text, body or message. HandoffAttempt has exactly three fields and its class field is asserted to be the closed FailureClass enum; a history entry carrying an undeclared class string is refused, as is one naming a fourth Provider. MEASURED EXCEPTION recorded: Handoff.Failure is a Failure whose Message is a string, reached only through that one named field. It is not free text in practice and that is asserted rather than assumed -- a 4096-character error text is capped at 256 bytes and a secret-shaped error text never reaches the message or the handoff.
